BiblicalUsage: Beth-Eden means house of delight, and it shows up once, in Amos 1:5, where the Lord says he will cut off the one who holds the sceptre from the house of Eden. The name never stands as a single word in the Hebrew text — it comes as two words, house and Eden, joined together. A pleasant name on a city that still fell under God's judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a fine name never saved a city, and Beth-Eden is proof of that.
